summary: Describes how to tunnel Frame Relay over L2TPv3, covering frame encapsulation, virtual-circuit creation and deletion, and status change notification. L2TPv3 tunnels data link protocols over IP networks. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4591 explains how to carry Frame Relay circuits over an IP network inside an L2TPv3 tunnel. Frame Relay traffic is made of frames with a small header naming the circuit and carrying a few status bits. The document says how those frames are wrapped for the tunnel, how each circuit gets its own session, how the two ends tell each other when a circuit comes up or goes down, and how they agree on the size of the Frame Relay header before any traffic flows.

subtitle: How to carry Frame Relay virtual circuits across an IP network using L2TPv3 pseudowires.

tldr.problem: A service provider with Frame Relay customers wanted to offer the same permanent virtual circuits across an IP network, but L2TPv3 had no defined way to carry Frame Relay.
tldr.mechanism: The document defines a Frame Relay pseudowire type, the signalling to create and delete a session for each permanent virtual circuit, the way the circuit state is reported, and the encapsulation of each Frame Relay frame inside the tunnel.
tldr.outcome: Each Frame Relay circuit maps one to one onto a pseudowire, and the two ends agree on the header length before traffic starts. RFC 4591 was later updated by RFC 5641.

today: RFC 4591 is a Proposed Standard from 2006 and has since been updated by RFC 5641. It remains the reference for carrying Frame Relay circuits over L2TPv3.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 3931 defines a base protocol for Layer 2 Tunneling over IP networks. This document defines the specifics necessary for tunneling Frame Relay over L2TPv3. Such emulated circuits are referred to as Frame Relay Pseudowires.

The protocol specifics defined here for L2TPv3 Frame Relay pseudowires operating in a virtual circuit to virtual circuit mode include those necessary for frame encapsulation, PVC creation and deletion, and status change notification. Frame Relay traffic may also be transported in a port-to-port or interface-to-interface fashion using HDLC pseudowires as defined in RFC 4349. Support for Switched Virtual Circuits and for Switched and Soft Permanent Virtual Circuits is outside the scope of this document. The reader is expected to be very familiar with the terminology and protocol constructs defined in RFC 3931.
sections.plainLanguage: This document covers the circuit-by-circuit case, where each customer circuit becomes its own tunnel. Carrying whole ports is a different document.

sections.title: PVC Status Notification and Session Establishment
sections.content:
To tunnel a Frame Relay circuit over IP using L2TPv3, an L2TPv3 control connection MUST first be established as described in RFC 3931. The Start-Control-Connection-Request and the corresponding reply MUST include the Frame Relay Data Link Connection Identifier pseudowire type of 0x0001 in the Pseudowire Capabilities List, which identifies the control connection as able to establish sessions for Frame Relay pseudowires. An endpoint MUST be able to identify itself uniquely in those two messages via a globally unique value, by default the structured Router ID AVP, though the unstructured Hostname AVP MAY also be used.

Provisioning a permanent virtual circuit results in establishment of an L2TP session via the standard three-way handshake described in RFC 3931. An endpoint MAY initiate the session immediately upon PVC creation, or wait until the PVC state transitions to ACTIVE, which delays the allocation of L2TP resources until it is really needed. The Pseudowire Type AVP, attribute type 68, MUST be present in the Incoming-Call-Request and MUST include the Frame Relay type of 0x0001. The Circuit Status AVP MUST be present in the request and the reply, and MAY be present in the Set Link Info message. The Frame Relay Header Length AVP MAY be present in the request and the reply.

The Remote End ID AVP MUST be present in the Incoming-Call-Request in order to identify the PVC, together with the identity of the endpoint itself, so that the session can be associated with it. The Remote End ID AVP is of opaque form and variable length, though one MUST at a minimum support use of an unstructured four-octet value that is known to both endpoints. As with the request, the reply is sent only after the PVC transitions to ACTIVE. If the far end had not been provisioned for the PVC identified in the request, a Call-Disconnect-Notify would have been returned immediately, indicating that the circuit was not provisioned or available at that endpoint. The initiating end SHOULD then exhibit a periodic retry mechanism, whose period and maximum number of retries MUST be configurable. An implementation MAY send a request or reply before a PVC is ACTIVE, as long as the Circuit Status AVP reflects that the PVC is INACTIVE and a Set Link Info message is sent when the PVC becomes ACTIVE. The Incoming-Call-Connected is the final stage, confirming receipt of the reply with acceptable parameters so that traffic can flow in both directions.

When a PVC is deleted at either end, the associated L2TP session MUST be torn down with the Call-Disconnect-Notify message. Three Frame Relay result codes are defined: 17, the PVC was deleted permanently and is no longer provisioned; 18, the PVC has been INACTIVE for an extended period of time; and 19, mismatched Frame Relay header length.

After establishment, the Set Link Info control message signals Frame Relay link status notifications between the endpoints. It is a single message sent over the L2TP control channel, and because it is delivered reliably no additional response is required. It MUST be sent any time there is a circuit status change that may be reported by any value identified in the Circuit Status AVP, the only exceptions being the initial request, reply and disconnect messages. An endpoint participating in the PVC status management procedures of ITU-T Q.933 Annex A MUST transmit a Set Link Info message including the Circuit Status AVP when it detects a change in the status of a local PVC. All sessions established by a given control connection use the L2TP Hello facility for session keepalive, which gives basic dead peer and path detection.
sections.plainLanguage: Each circuit gets its own tunnel session, set up with a three-message handshake once the circuit is active. After that, a control message tells the far end about any change in the circuit's state.

sections.title: Circuit Status and Header Length
sections.content:
Frame Relay circuit status is reported with the Circuit Status AVP defined in RFC 3931, attribute type 71. Its value is a 16-bit mask with the two least significant bits defined and the remaining bits reserved for future use. Reserved bits MUST be set to 0 by the sender and ignored by the receiver. The N, or New, bit indicates whether the status indication is for a new Frame Relay PVC, with 1 meaning new and 0 meaning existing. The A, or Active, bit indicates whether the PVC is ACTIVE, with 1 meaning active and 0 meaning inactive.

The Frame Relay Header Length AVP, attribute type 85, indicates the number of bytes in the Frame Relay header, and the two peer endpoints MUST agree on that length. It is exchanged during session negotiation, in the request and reply messages. If the other endpoint supports a different Frame Relay header length, the associated L2TP session MUST be torn down with a Call-Disconnect-Notify message with result code 19. If the AVP is not signalled, it MUST be assumed that the peer uses a 2-byte Frame Relay header. The attribute value is a 2-octet unsigned integer with two values defined: 2 for a two-octet Frame Relay header and 4 for a four-octet Frame Relay header. The AVP MAY be hidden, and the length before hiding is 8.
sections.plainLanguage: Two small pieces of information are exchanged before traffic starts: whether the circuit is up, and how long the Frame Relay header is. If the two ends disagree about the header length, the session is torn down rather than started.

sections.title: Encapsulation
sections.content:
The Frame Relay PDU is transported in its entirety, excluding the opening and closing HDLC flags and the frame check sequence. Bit stuffing is undone. The L2TPv3 session header is the one defined in RFC 3931. If sequencing or other features require the presence of an L2-specific sublayer, the default format defined in RFC 3931 MUST be used.

The Frame Relay header is defined in ITU-T Q.922. In IETF notation the two-octet header carries the high part of the DLCI, the command or response bit, a zero bit, the low part of the DLCI, and then the FECN, BECN, DE bits and a final bit set to 1. The four-octet header carries the same information in a wider form, with a longer DLCI.

The C/R bit is conveyed transparently and its value MUST NOT be changed by the endpoint. The FECN bit MAY be set by the endpoint to notify the receiving end user that the frames it receives have encountered congestion, and the bit must never be cleared by the endpoint. If the endpoint does not support FECN, it passes the bit unchanged. The BECN bit MAY be set to notify the receiving end user that the frames it transmits may encounter congestion, and again the bit must never be cleared. The DE bit MAY be set by a policing function to indicate that the frame SHOULD be discarded in preference to other frames in a congestion situation, and must never be cleared; if the endpoint does not support DE, it passes the bit unchanged.

The encapsulation of Frame Relay frames with the two-octet header is REQUIRED. The encapsulation with the four-octet header is OPTIONAL, and the three-octet header is outside the scope of the document.

Data packet sequencing MAY be enabled for Frame Relay pseudowires, using the mechanisms described in RFC 3931 to signal sequencing support. A pseudowire over L2TP MUST request the presence of the default L2-specific sublayer when sequencing is enabled. If the pseudowire is known to be carrying data that does not require packet order to be strictly maintained, such as IP, then sequencing SHOULD NOT be enabled.

With L2TPv3 as the tunneling protocol, the packet resulting from the encapsulation is N bytes longer than the Frame Relay frame without the opening and closing HDLC flags or the frame check sequence. The value of N depends on the session header fields: the flags, version and reserved fields take 4 octets for L2TPv3 over UDP only, the session ID takes 4 octets, the cookie size is 0, 4 or 8 octets, and the L2-specific sublayer is 0 or 4 octets when sequencing is used. The range for N is therefore 4 to 16 octets when L2TPv3 data messages are over IP, and 16 to 28 octets when they are over UDP. N does not include the IP header.
sections.plainLanguage: The Frame Relay frame is carried whole, minus the flag bytes and the checksum, which the far end recomputes. The bits that report congestion and priority pass through unchanged, and the endpoint may set them but never clear them.

sections.title: Applicability
sections.content:
The Frame Relay pseudowire emulation described in this document allows a service provider to offer a Frame Relay PVC-based service across an IP packet-switched network. A Frame Relay port-based service can be offered using RFC 4349.

The emulation has the following characteristics in relation to the native service. There is a one-to-one mapping between a Frame Relay PVC and a pseudowire, supporting bidirectional transport of variable length frames. The Frame Relay frame is transported in its entirety, including the DLCI and the C/R, FECN, BECN and DE bits, but excluding the opening and closing flags and the frame check sequence. The egress endpoint rewrites the DLCI and regenerates the frame check sequence.

Two-octet and four-octet address fields are supported, and the length is negotiated between the endpoints during session establishment. The availability or unavailability of the PVC is signalled with the Circuit Status AVP, and loss of connectivity between the endpoints can be detected by the L2TPv3 keepalive mechanism. These indications can be used to determine the PVC status to be signalled through the Q.933 procedures at the Frame Relay interface.

The maximum frame size that can be supported is limited by the packet-switched network MTU, unless fragmentation and reassembly is used. Sequencing may be enabled on the pseudowire to ensure that frames are delivered in order. Quality of Service characteristics, such as throughput, committed burst size, excess burst size and priority, can be provided by leveraging the quality of service features of the endpoints and of the underlying network.
sections.plainLanguage: Each customer circuit gets one tunnel. The far end rewrites the circuit number and recomputes the checksum. The largest frame that fits is limited by the size of the IP network's packets.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Frame Relay over L2TPv3 is subject to the security considerations defined in RFC 3931. There are no additional considerations specific to carrying Frame Relay that are not present for carrying other data link types.
sections.plainLanguage: Nothing extra is needed for Frame Relay. The general L2TPv3 security rules cover it.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content:
For the pseudowire type, the value 0x0001 is allocated by IANA for the Frame Relay DLCI pseudowire type, in the number space created as part of the publication of RFC 3931.

Three new L2TP result codes for the Call-Disconnect-Notify message are registered: 17, PVC was deleted permanently and is no longer provisioned; 18, PVC has been INACTIVE for an extended period of time; and 19, mismatched Frame Relay header length.

One new control message AVP is allocated, attribute type 85, the Frame Relay Header Length.
sections.plainLanguage: Three registrations: the pseudowire type number, three new error codes for a failed session, and the attribute number for the header length.

messages.note: Sent once the PVC is provisioned and ACTIVE. Status 0x03 means new and active.

messages.note: The far end confirms the parameters.

messages.note: The final stage, allowing bidirectional traffic.

fields.desc: High part of the DLCI, the circuit number.

fields.desc: Command or response bit. Passed through unchanged.

items.label: Mismatched header length
items.desc: The two ends disagree about the Frame Relay header length.
